subject: Construction and its material supply chain
reads: findings first, then what they mean, then what could be developed, then the specific evidence that would change a decision

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: these establishments or this employment exists here
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: Santa Fe County has an established construction economy: 547 establishments employing 2,981 people, 6.1% of all private employment the county publishes.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: this is how the local economy is composed, or how it has changed
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: It is predominantly specialty trade work: 315 specialty trade establishments employ 1,717 people, 58% of construction employment, averaging 5.5 employees each. Residential building adds 190 establishments and 849 employees.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: this kind of production requires these inputs
claims.basis_means: a national production relationship. It describes what an industry of this kind REQUIRES on average in the United States. That is real information about production, and it is not a statement about any local firm's purchases.
claims.statement: Fabricated metal products (NAICS 332) are construction's largest single intermediate input nationally: 16.3% of the $1,108,514m basket of intermediate purchases, ahead of nonmetallic minerals and wood. That basket is 48% of construction's $2,333,007m total industry output — the remainder is value added — so fabricated-metal inputs are equivalent to 7.7% of total construction industry output. TOTAL OUTPUT IS A PRODUCTION-ACCOUNTING MEASURE, not a firm's expense budget, so that second figure is a comparison against output and not a share of what construction firms spend.
claims.limits: a national production structure, and a COMMODITY CLASS. It establishes what construction of this kind requires on average in the United States. It is not an observation of anything bought in this county, and NAICS 332 covers many products, only some of which any given builder uses.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: these establishments or this employment exists here
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: Santa Fe has an observed presence in that same industry: 17 fabricated metal establishments (NAICS 332) employing 83. The largest published part is architectural and structural metals (NAICS 3323) — 6 establishments, 33 employees — which is the part of 332 most associated with building work.
claims.limits: a presence in NAICS 332, and within it 3323, is evidence of RELATED local manufacturing capability. It does not establish that these firms make the particular products Santa Fe construction buys, nor at the specification or volume it buys them.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: this is how the local economy is composed, or how it has changed
claims.basis_means: computed here from stated inputs by a stated recipe
claims.statement: That count is a floor, not a census. Published 4-digit detail accounts for 15 of 17 establishments and 71 of 83 employees; the remaining 2 establishments and up to 12 employees are withheld by disclosure rules, not absent from the county.
claims.limits: the source measures it and declined to publish it. A published parent BOUNDS what is hidden; the hidden value is never zero and never unbounded.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: these parts of the economy are connected -- labour, geography, infrastructure
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: The workforce is regional, not local: of 63,008 jobs in the county, 26,065 are filled by people living elsewhere, while 21,970 residents leave to work.
claims.limits: internal divided by resident workers. The denominator counts New Mexico residents working at New Mexico jobs, because LODES holds no record of a resident working in another state. Any such resident is missing from the denominator, so this figure is an UPPER BOUND on self-containment.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_KNOW
claims.asserts_means: this is how the local economy is composed, or how it has changed
claims.basis_means: computed here from stated inputs by a stated recipe
claims.statement: Construction pays $53,964 per worker against a county average of $52,618 — close to typical, not a high-wage enclave.

claims.question: WHAT_IT_MEANS
claims.asserts_means: this is how the local economy is composed, or how it has changed
claims.basis_means: computed here from stated inputs by a stated recipe
claims.statement: This is a small-firm industry. 547 establishments for 2,981 jobs is 5.4 employees each, so capacity is distributed across many small contractors rather than concentrated in a few. Coordination, not consolidation, is the lever that fits that structure.

claims.question: WHAT_IT_MEANS
claims.asserts_means: this is a development question the evidence makes it reasonable to pursue
claims.basis_means: a national production relationship. It describes what an industry of this kind REQUIRES on average in the United States. That is real information about production, and it is not a statement about any local firm's purchases.
claims.statement: Santa Fe has an observed presence in fabricated metal manufacturing, including the architectural and structural metals most associated with building work, in a county whose construction sector nationally-modelled input structure identifies that commodity class as its largest intermediate purchase. That is a related local capability sitting beside a known requirement, which makes regional sourcing and supplier-capacity investigations economically relevant.
claims.limits: the two halves are observed independently: one is a national input structure, the other a local establishment count. Nothing held connects them. Whether these firms make what these builders buy — and whether anyone already buys it — are the open questions below, not findings.

claims.question: WHAT_IT_MEANS
claims.asserts_means: these parts of the economy are connected -- labour, geography, infrastructure
claims.basis_means: computed here from stated inputs by a stated recipe
claims.statement: Construction labour is drawn from a multi-county shed. With self-containment at 63% at most, a workforce intervention scoped to county residents would miss a large share of the people doing the work.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_COULD_DEVELOP
claims.asserts_means: this is a development question the evidence makes it reasonable to pursue
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: Regional sourcing of fabricated metal. The buyers and a supplier base both exist in the county; the question is whether local fabrication can meet construction specifications, volumes and lead times. One round of conversations with a builder and a fabricator would settle the direction.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_COULD_DEVELOP
claims.asserts_means: this is a development question the evidence makes it reasonable to pursue
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: Capacity at the existing fabricators. 17 establishments and 83 employees is a small base against a construction sector of 2,981. If demand is real, the binding question is whether these firms can expand — equipment, workforce, premises — or whether the gap needs a new entrant — and the withheld detail means even that base is known only to a floor.

claims.question: WHAT_WE_COULD_DEVELOP
claims.asserts_means: this is a development question the evidence makes it reasonable to pursue
claims.basis_means: measured in this geography by a named source
claims.statement: Workforce development scoped to the labour shed rather than the county. Training and apprenticeship designed around where construction workers actually live would reach the workforce the industry employs.

claims.question: WHAT_WOULD_CHANGE_IT
claims.asserts_means: this buyer actually purchases from this supplier
claims.statement: Whether Santa Fe builders currently buy fabricated metal locally, and if not, why not — price, specification, lead time or capacity. Nothing held observes a purchase. This is what separates a sourcing opportunity from a sourcing assumption, and it is answered by asking buyers, not by more data.

claims.question: WHAT_WOULD_CHANGE_IT
claims.asserts_means: this would work commercially at a stated price and volume
claims.statement: What expansion would cost at the existing fabricators, and at what volume it pays back. Required before any capital commitment; not required to ask the sourcing question.

claims.question: WHAT_WOULD_CHANGE_IT
claims.asserts_means: these establishments or this employment exists here
claims.statement: Which products the local 332 firms actually make, and whether any match construction specifications. The commodity class is broad and the published detail is incomplete, so a directory check plus a short call sheet would establish what capability is really here.

confidence_note: Confidence attaches to a CLAIM, not to this investigation. Each claim carries the evidence that holds it up. A missing purchase observation limits the purchasing claim and nothing else.
